c: count_tokens("The sensor timed out.")   # 21 characters, 4 words
o: 5: the full stop is a token of its own
why: The pieces are The, ' sensor', ' timed', ' out' and '.'. A token is not a word.

q: Which is cheaper per character, and how many tokens does each have?
o: Both are 2 tokens: the long word is cut into a few big pieces
why: Common words and word parts are single tokens, so a long common word can be very cheap.

q: How many tokens do ten digits cost?
why: Numbers are cut into pieces of a few digits, so long numbers cost more than you may expect.

q: JSON has quotes, braces and colons. How many tokens?
why: The punctuation costs tokens too: a short JSON object is much more than its 4 words.

q: Do the two encodings give the same count?
o: No: 6 tokens with o200k_base and 18 with cl100k_base
why: Each model family has its own tokenizer. Count with the one that matches your model.

c: count_tokens("a <|endoftext|> b")   # a user typed a special token name
why: tiktoken refuses text that looks like a special token unless you say how to treat it. Decide on purpose what your app does.
